vulnerability.title: Undici fetch does not delete the Cookie and Host headers on a cross-origin redirect, leaking them to the redirect target

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.26.2 the cross-origin branch of httpRedirectFetch deletes cookie and host in addition to authorization; at the v5.19.0 snapshot only authorization is deleted. The change enters the release line exactly at the v5.26.2 tag commit 12a62187 and the tag commit's lib/fetch/index.js blob equals the fix commit's post-image.

vulnerability.category_l2: Credential leakage: cross-origin redirect in fetch keeps Cookie (and Host) request headers

critical_operation.description: httpRedirectFetch() handles step 13 of the fetch redirect algorithm: when the redirect target is not same-origin with the current URL it must delete the CORS non-wildcard request headers from the request's header list. At v5.19.0 the branch deletes only 'authorization' (line 1206) and leaves 'cookie' and 'host' in request.headersList. Undici does not implement forbidden request-header names (the Headers.append comment at lib/fetch/headers.js:232 says so explicitly), so a caller-supplied Cookie header survives Request construction and is therefore still present when mainFetch() reissues the request against the redirect target (line 1239, request.urlList.push(locationURL) at 1232). A server that answers with a 3xx Location to an attacker-controlled origin receives the victim's Cookie header. The v5.26.2 fix e041de35 adds request.headersList.delete('cookie') and request.headersList.delete('host') inside the same branch. CWE-200.

entry_point.description: Application code calls the exported fetch() (or Request/Client) with a Cookie header and follows an HTTP redirect to a different origin controlled by an attacker.

trace.description: Headers.append performs no forbidden-request-header filtering: the implementation note states that undici does not implement forbidden header names, so a Cookie header is stored

source_crosscheck.notes: CNA, NVD and both OSV views agree on CWE-200, on the '<5.26.2' affected range and on 5.26.2 as the fixed release; NVD's CPE versionEndExcluding is 5.26.2. The CNA publishes CVSS 3.1 3.9 Low and NVD carries the same vector as a Secondary metric, while NVD's Primary metric is 3.5 Low with a narrower vector; the base severity level (Low) is the same in all records, so no level disagreement exists. Local ancestry and blob mapping place the fix e041de3 exactly at v5.26.2, absent from v5.26.0/v5.26.1 and also absent from the v5.19.x line.

An independent reviewer must confirm e041de3 is the fix, is not an ancestor of v5.26.0/v5.26.1 and is contained in v5.26.2.

independent_corrections_accepted: Severity: NVD's Primary metric is 3.5 Low with CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N, while the CNA, the GitHub advisory, OSV and NVD's Secondary metric give 3.9 Low with CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L. Both published base scores are Low, so the level is consistent; the dossier records both scores and the CNA vector without re-scoring.
CWE: NVD's Primary weakness is NVD-CWE-noinfo, while the CNA, GitHub advisory and OSV assign CWE-200; the dossier records the CNA/GHSA value and this note.

Host qualification: at the v5.19.0 snapshot Host was also still forwarded, but on the 5.26.x line commit 470ee381 already deleted Host unconditionally before e041de3, so the fix's delete('host') is redundant there; the advisory text names only Cookie, and the recorded impact is the Cookie leak.

Cookie retention is explicit-header-only: the snapshot has no cookie jar (includeCredentials is TODO), so the leak requires the caller to set a Cookie header through RequestInit.headers, with redirect: 'follow' and a cross-origin Location.
Duplicate check: CVE-2022-31151/GHSA-q768-x9m6-m9qp is the same class in the legacy lib/handler/redirect.js (fixed 5.8.0); CVE-2023-23936 and CVE-2023-24807 are distinct 5.19.x advisories.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No fetch call, HTTP server or redirect was executed; the leak is established statically from the deletion logic and the advisory.
Only the 5.26.x line was inspected; other maintained branches and the 6.x fixes were not diffed.

The practical impact depends on the application passing a Cookie header through undici's fetch (or another dispatcher API on the same path) and following a redirect to an attacker-controlled origin; browser fetch normally forbids setting Cookie.
The Host header is also left in place, but the advisory and this dossier treat the Cookie leak as the principal issue.
NVD's Primary vector differs from the CNA vector (AC:L/PR:L/C:L/I:N/A:N vs AC:H/PR:H/C:L/I:L/A:L); the dossier records the CNA vector and both published scores, without re-scoring.
The reviewer confirmed snapshot blobs (tree 2712aff2, index.js ae60a5af, headers.js 634b81fc) against the inventory; no fetch call, HTTP server or redirect was executed.
The fix commit's delete('host') is redundant on the 5.26.x line because 470ee381 already removed Host; the Cookie deletion is the operative change for this advisory.
open_questions: Whether applications commonly set Cookie explicitly via RequestInit.headers (the advisory asserts this is possible in Node.js) was not surveyed.
